schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A INT, B INT);
q1: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
counterexample: INSERT INTO R (A, B) VALUES (1, NULL);
explanation: Q1 counts all rows in table R, while Q2 counts non-null values in column B. If B contains NULL values, the results will differ.
counterexample_dsp: A table with one row where B is NULL will cause Q1 to return 1 and Q2 to return 0.
q1_validation_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2_validation_sql: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
